units.leftText: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia to send a proclamation throughout his kingdom and to put it in writing as follows:
units.rightText: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of Jehovah by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, Jehovah stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,

units.leftText: “This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, who has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, has appointed me to build a house for Him at Jerusalem in Judah.
units.rightText: Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath Jehovah, the God of heaven, given me; and he hath charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

units.leftText: Whoever among you belongs to His people, may his God be with him, and may he go to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel; He is the God who is in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Whosoever there is among you of all his people, his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of Jehovah, the God of Israel (he is God), which is in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And let every survivor, wherever he lives, be assisted by the men of that region with silver, gold, goods, and livestock, along with a freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.’”
units.rightText: And whosoever is left, in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, besides the freewill-offering for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: So the family heads of Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and Levites— everyone whose spirit God had stirred— prepared to go up and rebuild the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Then rose up the heads of fathers’ houses of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, even all whose spirit God had stirred to go up to build the house of Jehovah which is in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And all their neighbors supported them with articles of silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with valuables, in addition to all their freewill offerings. Cyrus Restores the Holy Vessels
units.rightText: And all they that were round about them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with beasts, and with precious things, besides all that was willingly offered.

units.leftText: King Cyrus also brought out the articles belonging to the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem and placed in the temple of his gods.
units.rightText: Also Cyrus the king brought forth the vessels of the house of Jehovah, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought forth out of Jerusalem, and had put in the house of his gods;

units.leftText: Cyrus king of Persia had them brought out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.
units.rightText: even those did Cyrus king of Persia bring forth by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and numbered them unto Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.

units.rightText: Now these are the children of the province, that went up out of the captivity of those that had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon, and that returned unto Jerusalem and Judah, every one unto his city;

units.leftText: These men searched for their family records, but they could not find them and so were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.
units.rightText: These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they deemed polluted and put from the priesthood.

units.leftText: The governor ordered them not to eat the most holy things until there was a priest to consult the Urim and Thummim.

units.leftText: When they arrived at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some of the heads of the families gave freewill offerings to rebuild the house of God on its original site.
units.rightText: And some of the heads of fathers’ houses, when they came to the house of Jehovah which is in Jerusalem, offered willingly for the house of God to set it up in its place:

units.leftText: According to their ability, they gave to the treasury for this work 61,000 darics of gold, 5,000 minas of silver, and 100 priestly garments.
units.rightText: they gave after their ability into the treasury of the work threescore and one thousand darics of gold, and five thousand pounds of silver, and one hundred priests’ garments.
leftNotes: 2:69 Or 61,000 gold drachmas; that is, approximately 1,129.7 pounds or 512.4 kilograms of gold coins
2:69 5,000 minas is approximately 3.14 tons or 2.85 metric tons of silver.

units.leftText: So the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants, along with some of the people, settled in their own towns; and the rest of the Israelites settled in their towns.
units.rightText: So the priests, and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinim, dwelt in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
leftNotes: 2:70 Or all Israel

units.leftText: By the seventh month, the Israelites had settled in their towns, and the people assembled as one man in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And when the seventh month was come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, along with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his associates, began to build the altar of the God of Israel to sacrifice burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the Law of Moses the man of God.
units.rightText: Then stood up Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and builded the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt-offerings thereon, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.
leftNotes: 3:2 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; also in verse 8; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: They set up the altar on its foundation and sacrificed burnt offerings on it to the LORD — both the morning and evening burnt offerings — even though they feared the people of the land.
units.rightText: And they set the altar upon its base; for fear was upon them because of the peoples of the countries: and they offered burnt-offerings thereon unto Jehovah, even burnt-offerings morning and evening.

units.leftText: They also celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles in accordance with what is written, and they offered burnt offerings daily based on the number prescribed for each day.
units.rightText: And they kept the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt-offerings by number, according to the ordinance, as the duty of every day required;
leftNotes: 3:4 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; also translated as the Feast of Booths or the Feast of Shelters and originally called the Feast of Ingathering(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16* and Exodus 34:22).

units.leftText: After that, they presented the regular burnt offerings and those for New Moons and for all the appointed sacred feasts of the LORD, as well as all the freewill offerings brought to the LORD.
units.rightText: and afterward the continual burnt-offering, and the offerings of the new moons, and of all the set feasts of Jehovah that were consecrated, and of every one that willingly offered a freewill-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: On the first day of the seventh month, the Israelites began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, although the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not been laid.
units.rightText: From the first day of the seventh month began they to offer burnt-offerings unto Jehovah: but the foundation of the temple of Jehovah was not yet laid.

units.leftText: They gave money to the masons and carpenters, and food and drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea, as authorized by Cyrus king of Persia. Temple Restoration Begins
units.rightText: They gave money also unto the masons, and to the carpenters; and food, and drink, and oil, unto them of Sidon, and to them of Tyre, to bring cedar-trees from Lebanon to the sea, unto Joppa, according to the grant that they had of Cyrus king of Persia.

units.leftText: In the second month of the second year after they had arrived at the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of their associates including the priests, the Levites, and all who had returned to Jerusalem from the captivity, began the work. They appointed Levites twenty years of age or older to supervise the construction of the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: Now in the second year of their coming unto the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, began Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brethren the priests and the Levites, and all they that were come out of the captivity unto Jerusalem, and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: So Jeshua and his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons (descendants of Yehudah), and the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers — all Levites — joined together to supervise those working on the house of God.
units.rightText: Then stood Jeshua with his sons and his brethren, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, together, to have the oversight of the workmen in the house of God: the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their brethren the Levites.
leftNotes: 3:9 Hebrew sons of Judah; that is, most likely, sons of Yehudah, another name for Hodevah or Hodaviah; see Ezra 2:40|EZR 2:40* and Nehemiah 7:43.

units.leftText: When the builders had laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites (the sons of Asaph) with cymbals, took their positions to praise the LORD, as David king of Israel had prescribed.
units.rightText: And when the builders laid the foundation of the temple of Jehovah, they set the priests in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise Jehovah, after the order of David king of Israel.

units.leftText: And they sang responsively with praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “For He is good; for His loving devotion to Israel endures forever.” Then all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.
units.rightText: And they sang one to another in praising and giving thanks unto Jehovah, saying, For he is good, for his lovingkindness endureth for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised Jehovah, because the foundation of the house of Jehovah was laid.
leftNotes: 3:11 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: But many of the older priests, Levites, and family heads who had seen the first temple wept loudly when they saw the foundation of this temple. Still, many others shouted joyfully.
units.rightText: But many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers’ houses, the old men that had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice; and many shouted aloud for joy:

units.leftText: The people could not distinguish the shouts of joy from the sound of weeping, because the people were making so much noise. And the sound was heard from afar.
units.rightText: so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people; for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard afar off.

units.leftText: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel,
units.rightText: Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple unto Jehovah, the God of Israel;

units.leftText: they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the families, saying, “Let us build with you because, like you, we seek your God and have been sacrificing to Him since the time of King Esar-haddon of Assyria, who brought us here.”
units.rightText: then they drew near to Zerubbabel, and to the heads of fathers’ houses, and said unto them, Let us build with you; for we seek your God, as ye do; and we sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar-haddon king of Assyria, who brought us up hither.

units.leftText: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other heads of the families of Israel replied, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God, since we alone must build it for the LORD, the God of Israel, as Cyrus king of Persia has commanded us.”
units.rightText: But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of fathers’ houses of Israel, said unto them, Ye have nothing to do with us in building a house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto Jehovah, the God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.

units.leftText: Then the people of the land set out to discourage the people of Judah and make them afraid to build.
units.rightText: Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building,

units.leftText: They hired counselors against them to frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus king of Persia and down to the reign of Darius king of Persia. Opposition under Xerxes and Artaxerxes
units.rightText: and hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.

units.leftText: At the beginning of the reign of Xerxes, an accusation was lodged against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, wrote they an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 4:6 Hebrew Ahasuerus

units.leftText: And in the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his associates wrote a letter to Artaxerxes. It was written in Aramaic and then translated.
units.rightText: And in the days of Artaxerxes wrote Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions, unto Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in the Syrian character, and set forth in the Syrian tongue.
leftNotes: 4:7 The original text of Ezra 4:8|EZR 4:8* through Ezra 6:18 is in Aramaic.

units.leftText: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote the letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows:
units.rightText: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king in this sort:

units.leftText: From Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates— the judges and officials over Tripolis, Persia, Erech and Babylon, the Elamites of Susa,
units.rightText: then wrote Rehum the chancellor, and Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their companions, the Dinaites, and the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Shushanchites, the Dehaites, the Elamites,

units.leftText: and the rest of the peoples whom the great and honorable Ashurbanipal deported and settled in the cities of Samaria and elsewhere west of the Euphrates.
units.rightText: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar brought over, and set in the city of Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River, and so forth.
leftNotes: 4:10 Aramaic Osnappar, another name for Ashurbanipal
4:10 Aramaic beyond the River; also in verses 11, 16, 17, and 20

units.leftText: (This is the text of the letter they sent to him.) To King Artaxerxes, From your servants, the men west of the Euphrates:
units.rightText: This is the copy of the letter that they sent unto Artaxerxes the king: Thy servants the men beyond the River, and so forth.

units.leftText: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came from you to us have returned to Jerusalem and are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They are restoring its walls and repairing its foundations.
units.rightText: Be it known unto the king, that the Jews that came up from thee are come to us unto Jerusalem; they are building the rebellious and the bad city, and have finished the walls, and repaired the foundations.

units.leftText: Let it now be known to the king that if that city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, they will not pay tribute, duty, or toll, and the royal treasury will suffer.
units.rightText: Be it known now unto the king, that, if this city be builded, and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it will be hurtful unto the kings.

units.leftText: Now because we are in the service of the palace and it is not fitting for us to allow the king to be dishonored, we have sent to inform the king
units.rightText: Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not meet for us to see the king’s dishonor, therefore have we sent and certified the king;
leftNotes: 4:14 Literally because the salt of the palace is our salt

units.leftText: that a search should be made of the record books of your fathers. In these books you will discover and verify that the city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, inciting sedition from ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.
units.rightText: that search may be made in the book of the records of thy fathers: so shalt thou find in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful unto kings and provinces, and that they have moved sedition within the same of old time; for which cause was this city laid waste.

units.leftText: We advise the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, you will have no dominion west of the Euphrates. The Decree of Artaxerxes
units.rightText: We certify the king that, if this city be builded, and the walls finished, by this means thou shalt have no portion beyond the River.

units.leftText: Then the king sent this reply: To Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of your associates living in Samaria and elsewhere in the region west of the Euphrates: Greetings.
units.rightText: Then sent the king an answer unto Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companions that dwell in Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River: Peace, and so forth.

units.leftText: The letter you sent us has been translated and read in my presence.
units.rightText: The letter which ye sent unto us hath been plainly read before me.

units.leftText: I issued a decree, and a search was conducted. It was discovered that this city has revolted against kings from ancient times, engaging in rebellion and sedition.
units.rightText: And I decreed, and search hath been made, and it is found that this city of old time hath made insurrection against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been made therein.

units.leftText: And mighty kings have ruled over Jerusalem and exercised authority over the whole region west of the Euphrates; and tribute, duty, and toll were paid to them.
units.rightText: There have been mighty kings also over Jerusalem, who have ruled over all the country beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll, was paid unto them.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, issue an order for these men to stop, so that this city will not be rebuilt until I so order.
units.rightText: Make ye now a decree to cause these men to cease, and that this city be not builded, until a decree shall be made by me.

units.leftText: See that you do not neglect this matter. Why allow this threat to increase and the royal interests to suffer?
units.rightText: And take heed that ye be not slack herein: why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?

units.leftText: When the text of the letter from King Artaxerxes was read to Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they went immediately to the Jews in Jerusalem and forcibly stopped them.
units.rightText: Then when the copy of king Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went in haste to Jerusalem unto the Jews, and made them to cease by force and power.

units.leftText: Thus the construction of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
units.rightText: Then ceased the work of the house of God which is at Jerusalem; and it ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

units.leftText: Later, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
units.rightText: Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied unto the Jews that were in Judah and Jerusalem; in the name of the God of Israel prophesied they unto them.

units.leftText: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak rose up and began to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem. And the prophets of God were with them, helping them.
units.rightText: Then rose up Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and began to build the house of God which is at Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
leftNotes: 5:2 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: At that time Tattenai the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates went to the Jews and asked, “Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?”
units.rightText: At the same time came to them Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai, and their companions, and said thus unto them, Who gave you a decree to build this house, and to finish this wall?
leftNotes: 5:3 Aramaic the governor beyond the River; also in verse 6

units.leftText: They also asked, “What are the names of the men who are constructing this building?”
units.rightText: Then we told them after this manner, what the names of the men were that were making this building.
leftNotes: 5:4 LXX and Syriac; Aramaic Then we told them,

units.leftText: But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, so that they were not stopped until a report was sent to Darius and written instructions about this matter were returned. Tattenai’s Letter to Darius
units.rightText: But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, and they did not make them cease, till the matter should come to Darius, and then answer should be returned by letter concerning it.

units.leftText: This is the text of the letter that Tattenai the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates, the officials in the region, sent to King Darius.
units.rightText: The copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai, and his companions the Apharsachites, who were beyond the River, sent unto Darius the king;

units.leftText: The report they sent him read as follows: To King Darius: All peace.
units.rightText: they sent a letter unto him, wherein was written thus: Unto Darius the king, all peace.

units.leftText: Let it be known to the king that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. The people are rebuilding it with large stones and placing timbers in the walls. This work is being carried out diligently and is prospering in their hands.
units.rightText: Be it known unto the king, that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is builded with great stones, and timber is laid in the walls; and this work goeth on with diligence and prospereth in their hands.

units.leftText: So we questioned the elders and asked, “Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?”
units.rightText: Then asked we those elders, and said unto them thus, Who gave you a decree to build this house, and to finish this wall?

units.leftText: We also asked for their names, so that we could write down the names of their leaders for your information.
units.rightText: We asked them their names also, to certify thee, that we might write the names of the men that were at the head of them.
leftNotes: 5:10 Aramaic the names of the men at their heads

units.leftText: And this is the answer they returned:
units.rightText: And thus they returned us answer, saying, We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and are building the house that was builded these many years ago, which a great king of Israel builded and finished.

units.leftText: But since our fathers angered the God of heaven, He delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean who destroyed this temple and carried away the people to Babylon.
units.rightText: But after that our fathers had provoked the God of heaven unto wrath, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house, and carried the people away into Babylon.

units.leftText: In the first year of his reign, however, Cyrus king of Babylon issued a decree to rebuild this house of God.
units.rightText: But in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree to build this house of God.

units.leftText: He also removed from the temple of Babylon the gold and silver articles belonging to the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken and carried there from the temple in Jerusalem. King Cyrus gave these articles to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he appointed governor
units.rightText: And the gold and silver vessels also of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple that was in Jerusalem, and brought into the temple of Babylon, those did Cyrus the king take out of the temple of Babylon, and they were delivered unto one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor;
leftNotes: 5:14 Or palace

units.leftText: and instructed, ‘Take these articles, put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its original site.’
units.rightText: and he said unto him, Take these vessels, go, put them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be builded in its place.

units.leftText: So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundation of the house of God in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been under construction, but it has not yet been completed.”
units.rightText: Then came the same Sheshbazzar, and laid the foundations of the house of God which is in Jerusalem: and since that time even until now hath it been in building, and yet it is not completed.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, if it pleases the king, let a search be made of the royal archives in Babylon to see if King Cyrus did indeed issue a decree to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision in this matter.
units.rightText: Now therefore, if it seem good to the king, let there be search made in the king’s treasure-house, which is there at Babylon, whether it be so, that a decree was made of Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem; and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.

units.leftText: Thus King Darius ordered a search of the archives stored in the treasury of Babylon.
units.rightText: Then Darius the king made a decree, and search was made in the house of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon.

units.leftText: And a scroll was found in the fortress of Ecbatana, in the province of Media, with the following written on it: Memorandum:
units.rightText: And there was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of Media, a roll, and therein was thus written for a record:

units.leftText: In the first year of King Cyrus, he issued a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem:
units.rightText: In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: Concerning the house of God at Jerusalem, let the house be builded, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let the foundations thereof be strongly laid; the height thereof threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof threescore cubits;

units.leftText: with three layers of cut stones and one of timbers. The costs are to be paid from the royal treasury.
units.rightText: with three courses of great stones, and a course of new timber: and let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.

units.leftText: Furthermore, the gold and silver articles of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, must also be returned to the temple in Jerusalem and deposited in the house of God.
units.rightText: And also let the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took forth out of the temple which is at Jerusalem, and brought unto Babylon, be restored, and brought again unto the temple which is at Jerusalem, every one to its place; and thou shalt put them in the house of God.

units.leftText: Therefore Darius decreed: To Tattenai governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and your associates and officials in the region:
units.rightText: Now therefore, Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and your companions the Apharsachites, who are beyond the River, be ye far from thence:
leftNotes: 6:6 Aramaic governor beyond the River; similarly in verses 8 and 13

units.leftText: Leave this work on the house of God alone. Let the governor and elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its original site.
units.rightText: let the work of this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God in its place.

units.leftText: I hereby decree what you must do for these elders of the Jews who are rebuilding this house of God:
units.rightText: Moreover I make a decree what ye shall do to these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the River, expenses be given with all diligence unto these men, that they be not hindered.

units.leftText: Whatever is needed— young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil, as requested by the priests in Jerusalem— must be given to them daily without fail.
units.rightText: And that which they have need of, both young bullocks, and rams, and lambs, for burnt-offerings to the God of heaven; also wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the word of the priests that are at Jerusalem, let it be given them day by day without fail;

units.leftText: Then they will be able to offer sacrifices of a sweet aroma to the God of heaven and to pray for the lives of the king and his sons.
units.rightText: that they may offer sacrifices of sweet savor unto the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king, and of his sons.

units.leftText: I also decree that if any man interferes with this directive, a beam is to be torn from his house and raised up, and he is to be impaled on it. And his own house shall be made a pile of rubble for this offense.
units.rightText: Also I have made a decree, that whosoever shall alter this word, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and fastened thereon; and let his house be made a dunghill for this:
leftNotes: 6:11 Literally shall be made a dunghill because of this

units.leftText: May God, who has caused His Name to dwell there, overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter this decree or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued the decree. Let it be carried out with diligence. The Temple Completed
units.rightText: and the God that hath caused his name to dwell there overthrow all kings and peoples that shall put forth their hand to alter the same, to destroy this house of God which is at Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree; let it be done with all diligence.

units.leftText: In response, Tattenai the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates diligently carried out what King Darius had decreed.
units.rightText: Then Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their companions, because that Darius the king had sent, did accordingly with all diligence.

units.leftText: So the Jewish elders built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo.
units.rightText: And the elders of the Jews builded and prospered, through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. And they builded and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the decree of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

units.leftText: And this temple was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius. Dedication of the Temple
units.rightText: And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
leftNotes: 6:15 Adar is the twelfth month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of February and March.

units.leftText: Then the people of Israel — the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the exiles — celebrated the dedication of the house of God with joy.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel, the priests and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of God with joy.

units.leftText: For the dedication of the house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and a sin offering for all Israel of twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel.
units.rightText: And they offered at the dedication of this house of God a hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin-offering for all Israel, twelve he-goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

units.leftText: They also appointed the priests by their divisions and the Levites by their groups to the service of God in Jerusalem, according to what is written in the Book of Moses. The Returned Exiles Keep the Passover
units.rightText: And they set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, for the service of God, which is at Jerusalem; as it is written in the book of Moses.

units.leftText: On the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles kept the Passover.
units.rightText: And the children of the captivity kept the passover upon the fourteenth day of the first month.

units.leftText: All the priests and Levites had purified themselves and were ceremonially clean.
units.rightText: For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were pure: and they killed the passover for all the children of the captivity, and for their brethren the priests, and for themselves.

units.leftText: The Israelites who had returned from exile ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel that were come again out of the captivity, and all such as had separated themselves unto them from the filthiness of the nations of the land, to seek Jehovah, the God of Israel, did eat,
leftNotes: 6:21 Or nations

units.leftText: For seven days they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy, because the LORD had made them joyful and turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel.
units.rightText: and kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Jehovah had made them joyful, and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.
leftNotes: 6:22 That is, the seven-day period after the Passover during which no leaven may be eaten; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: Many years later, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
units.rightText: Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
leftNotes: 7:1 Literally After these things

units.leftText: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
units.rightText: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,

units.leftText: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
units.rightText: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,

units.leftText: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
units.rightText: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,

units.leftText: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest—
units.rightText: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest—

units.leftText: this Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given.
units.rightText: this Ezra went up from Babylon. And he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which Jehovah, the God of Israel, had given; and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of Jehovah his God upon him.

units.leftText: So in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, he went up to Jerusalem with some of the Israelites, including priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
units.rightText: And there went up some of the children of Israel, and of the priests, and the Levites, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinim, unto Jerusalem, in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
leftNotes: 7:7 Hebrew Nethinim; also in verse 24

units.leftText: Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king.
units.rightText: And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.

units.leftText: He had begun the journey from Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, for the gracious hand of his God was upon him.
units.rightText: For upon the first day of the first month began he to go up from Babylon; and on the first day of the fifth month came he to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.

units.leftText: For Ezra had set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, to practice it, and to teach its statutes and ordinances in Israel. Artaxerxes’ Letter for Ezra
units.rightText: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the law of Jehovah, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and ordinances.

units.leftText: This is the text of the letter King Artaxerxes had given to Ezra the priest and scribe, an expert in the commandments and statutes of the LORD to Israel:
units.rightText: Now this is the copy of the letter that the king Artaxerxes gave unto Ezra the priest, the scribe, even the scribe of the words of the commandments of Jehovah, and of his statutes to Israel:
leftNotes: 7:11 The original text of Ezra 7:12–26|EZR 7:12-26* is in Aramaic.

units.leftText: Artaxerxes, king of kings. To Ezra the priest, the scribe of the Law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
units.rightText: Artaxerxes, king of kings, unto Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, perfect and so forth.
leftNotes: 7:12 Aramaic Perfect now (probably a greeting)

units.leftText: I hereby decree that any volunteers among the Israelites in my kingdom, including the priests and Levites, may go up with you to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: I make a decree, that all they of the people of Israel, and their priests and the Levites, in my realm, that are minded of their own free will to go to Jerusalem, go with thee.

units.leftText: You are sent by the king and his seven counselors to evaluate Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God, which is in your hand.
units.rightText: Forasmuch as thou art sent of the king and his seven counsellors, to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem, according to the law of thy God which is in thy hand,

units.leftText: Moreover, you are to take with you the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
units.rightText: and to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counsellors have freely offered unto the God of Israel, whose habitation is in Jerusalem,

units.leftText: together with all the silver and gold you may find in all the province of Babylon, as well as the freewill offerings of the people and priests to the house of their God in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: and all the silver and gold that thou shalt find in all the province of Babylon, with the freewill-offering of the people, and of the priests, offering willingly for the house of their God which is in Jerusalem;

units.leftText: With this money, therefore, you are to buy as many bulls, rams, and lambs as needed, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and offer them on the altar at the house of your God in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: therefore thou shalt with all diligence buy with this money bullocks, rams, lambs, with their meal-offerings and their drink-offerings, and shalt offer them upon the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: You and your brothers may do whatever seems best with the rest of the silver and gold, according to the will of your God.
units.rightText: And whatsoever shall seem good to thee and to thy brethren to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, that do ye after the will of your God.

units.leftText: You must deliver to the God of Jerusalem all the articles given to you for the service of the house of your God.
units.rightText: And the vessels that are given thee for the service of the house of thy God, deliver thou before the God of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And if anything else is needed for the house of your God that you may have occasion to supply, you may pay for it from the royal treasury.
units.rightText: And whatsoever more shall be needful for the house of thy God, which thou shalt have occasion to bestow, bestow it out of the king’s treasure-house.

units.leftText: I, King Artaxerxes, decree to all the treasurers west of the Euphrates: Whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, may require of you, it must be provided promptly,
units.rightText: And I, even I Artaxerxes the king, do make a decree to all the treasurers that are beyond the River, that whatsoever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, shall require of you, it be done with all diligence,
leftNotes: 7:21 Aramaic beyond the River; also in verse 25

units.leftText: up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of olive oil, and salt without limit.
units.rightText: unto a hundred talents of silver, and to a hundred measures of wheat, and to a hundred baths of wine, and to a hundred baths of oil, and salt without prescribing how much.
leftNotes: 7:22 100 talents is approximately 3.77 tons or 3.42 metric tons of silver.
7:22 100 cors is approximately 624 bushels or 22,000 liters (probably about 19.2 tons or 17.4 metric tons of wheat).
7:22 100 baths is approximately 580 gallons or 2,200 liters of wine.
7:22 Or 100 baths of oil; that is, approximately 580 gallons or 2,200 liters

units.leftText: Whatever is commanded by the God of heaven must be done diligently for His house. For why should wrath fall on the realm of the king and his sons?
units.rightText: Whatsoever is commanded by the God of heaven, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?

units.leftText: And be advised that you have no authority to impose tribute, duty, or toll on any of the priests, Levites, singers, doorkeepers, temple servants, or other servants of this house of God.
units.rightText: Also we certify you, that touching any of the priests and Levites, the singers, porters, Nethinim, or servants of this house of God, it shall not be lawful to impose tribute, custom, or toll, upon them.

units.leftText: And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God, which you possess, are to appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people west of the Euphrates — all who know the laws of your God. And you are to teach these laws to anyone who does not know them.
units.rightText: And thou, Ezra, after the wisdom of thy God that is in thy hand, appoint magistrates and judges, who may judge all the people that are beyond the River, all such as know the laws of thy God; and teach ye him that knoweth them not.

units.leftText: If anyone does not keep the law of your God and the law of the king, let a strict judgment be executed against him, whether death, banishment, confiscation of property, or imprisonment. Ezra Blesses God
units.rightText: And whosoever will not do the law of thy God, and the law of the king, let judgment be executed upon him with all diligence, whether it be unto death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.

units.leftText: Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put into the heart of the king to so honor the house of the LORD in Jerusalem,
units.rightText: Blessed be Jehovah, the God of our fathers, who hath put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the house of Jehovah which is in Jerusalem;

units.leftText: and who has shown me favor before the king, his counselors, and all his powerful officials. And because the hand of the LORD my God was upon me, I took courage and gathered the leaders of Israel to return with me.
units.rightText: and hath extended lovingkindness unto me before the king, and his counsellors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. And I was strengthened according to the hand of Jehovah my God upon me, and I gathered together out of Israel chief men to go up with me.

units.leftText: These are the family heads and genealogical records of those who returned with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:
units.rightText: Now these are the heads of their fathers’ houses, and this is the genealogy of them that went up with me from Babylon, in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:

units.leftText: from the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; from the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel;
units.rightText: Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel. Of the sons of David, Hattush.

units.leftText: of the descendants of Shecaniah; from the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him were registered 150 men;
units.rightText: Of the sons of Shecaniah, of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah; and with him were reckoned by genealogy of the males a hundred and fifty.

units.leftText: from the descendants of Pahath-Moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him 200 men;
units.rightText: Of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah; and with him two hundred males.

units.leftText: from the descendants of Zattu, Shecaniah son of Jahaziel, and with him 300 men;
units.rightText: Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel; and with him three hundred males.
leftNotes: 8:5 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Esdras 8:32|8:32*); Hebrew from the descendants of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel

units.leftText: from the descendants of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him 50 men;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan; and with him fifty males.

units.leftText: from the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him 70 men;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah; and with him seventy males.

units.leftText: from the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him 80 men;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael; and with him fourscore males.

units.leftText: from the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him 218 men;
units.rightText: Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel; and with him two hundred and eighteen males.

units.leftText: from the descendants of Bani, Shelomith son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 men;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah; and with him a hundred and threescore males.
leftNotes: 8:10 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Esdras 8:36|8:36*); Hebrew from the descendants of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah

units.leftText: from the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him 28 men;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai; and with him twenty and eight males.

units.leftText: from the descendants of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan; and with him a hundred and ten males.

units.leftText: from the later descendants of Adonikam, these were their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them 60 men;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Adonikam, that were the last; and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah; and with them threescore males.
leftNotes: 8:13 Or the last

units.leftText: and from the descendants of Bigvai, both Uthai and Zaccur, and with them 70 men. Ezra Sends for the Levites
units.rightText: And of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud; and with them seventy males.
leftNotes: 8:14 LXX, Syriac, and an alternate MT reading; the other alternate reads Zabbud.

units.leftText: Now I assembled these exiles at the canal that flows to Ahava, and we camped there three days. And when I searched among the people and priests, I found no Levites there.
units.rightText: And I gathered them together to the river that runneth to Ahava; and there we encamped three days: and I viewed the people, and the priests, and found there none of the sons of Levi.

units.leftText: Then I summoned the leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, as well as the teachers Joiarib and Elnathan.
units.rightText: Then sent I for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan, and for Jarib, and for Elnathan, and for Nathan, and for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, chief men; also for Joiarib, and for Elnathan, who were teachers.
leftNotes: 8:16 Elnathan appears three times in verse, either as a repetition for emphasis or as a record of multiple men with this name.

units.leftText: And I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, with a message for him and his kinsmen, the temple servants at Casiphia, that they should bring to us ministers for the house of our God.
units.rightText: And I sent them forth unto Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia; and I told them what they should say unto Iddo, and his brethren the Nethinim, at the place Casiphia, that they should bring unto us ministers for the house of our God.
leftNotes: 8:17 Hebrew the Nethinim; also in verse 20

units.leftText: And since the gracious hand of our God was upon us, they brought us Sherebiah— a man of insight from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi, the son of Israel— along with his sons and brothers, 18 men;
units.rightText: And according to the good hand of our God upon us they brought us a man of discretion, of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel; and Sherebiah, with his sons and his brethren, eighteen;

units.leftText: also Hashabiah, together with Jeshaiah, from the descendants of Merari, and his brothers and their sons, 20 men.
units.rightText: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brethren and their sons, twenty;

units.leftText: They also brought 220 of the temple servants, all designated by name. David and the officials had appointed them to assist the Levites. Fasting for Protection
units.rightText: and of the Nethinim, whom David and the princes had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty Nethinim: all of them were mentioned by name.

units.leftText: And there by the Ahava Canal I proclaimed a fast, so that we might humble ourselves before our God and ask Him for a safe journey for us and our children, with all our possessions.
units.rightText: Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek of him a straight way for us, and for our little ones, and for all our substance.

units.leftText: For I was ashamed to ask the king for an escort of soldiers and horsemen to protect us from our enemies on the road, since we had told him, “The hand of our God is gracious to all who seek Him, but His great anger is against all who forsake Him.”
units.rightText: For I was ashamed to ask of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy in the way, because we had spoken unto the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all them that seek him, for good; but his power and his wrath is against all them that forsake him.

units.leftText: So we fasted and petitioned our God about this, and He granted our request. Priests to Guard the Offerings
units.rightText: So we fasted and besought our God for this: and he was entreated of us.

units.leftText: Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, together with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers,
units.rightText: Then I set apart twelve of the chiefs of the priests, even Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brethren with them,

units.leftText: and I weighed out to them the contribution of silver and gold and the articles that the king, his counselors, his leaders, and all the Israelites there had offered for the house of our God.
units.rightText: and weighed unto them the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, even the offering for the house of our God, which the king, and his counsellors, and his princes, and all Israel there present, had offered:

units.leftText: I weighed out into their hands 650 talents of silver, articles of silver weighing 100 talents, 100 talents of gold,
units.rightText: I weighed into their hand six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and silver vessels a hundred talents; of gold a hundred talents;
leftNotes: 8:26 650 talents is approximately 24.5 tons or 22.2 metric tons of silver.
8:26 100 talents is approximately 3.77 tons or 3.42 metric tons of silver articles.
8:26 100 talents is approximately 3.77 tons or 3.42 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: 20 gold bowls valued at 1,000 darics, and two articles of fine polished bronze, as precious as gold.
units.rightText: and twenty bowls of gold, of a thousand darics; and two vessels of fine bright brass, precious as gold.
leftNotes: 8:27 Or worth 1,000 drachmas; that is, approximately 18.5 pounds or 8.4 kilograms of gold

units.leftText: Then I told them, “You are holy to the LORD, and these articles are holy. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.
units.rightText: And I said unto them, Ye are holy unto Jehovah, and the vessels are holy; and the silver and the gold are a freewill-offering unto Jehovah, the God of your fathers.

units.leftText: Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the chambers of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem before the leading priests, Levites, and heads of the Israelite families.”
units.rightText: Watch ye, and keep them, until ye weigh them before the chiefs of the priests and the Levites, and the princes of the fathers’ houses of Israel, at Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: So the priests and Levites took charge of the silver and gold and sacred articles that had been weighed out to be taken to the house of our God in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold, and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem unto the house of our God.

units.leftText: On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the Ahava Canal to go to Jerusalem, and the hand of our God was upon us to protect us from the hands of the enemies and bandits along the way. Arrival in Jerusalem
units.rightText: Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go unto Jerusalem: and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and the lier-in-wait by the way.

units.leftText: So we arrived at Jerusalem and rested there for three days.
units.rightText: And we came to Jerusalem, and abode there three days.

units.leftText: On the fourth day, in the house of our God, we weighed out the silver and gold and sacred articles into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, along with the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
units.rightText: And on the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest (and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas; and with them was Jozabad the son of Jeshua, and Noadiah the son of Binnui, the Levites)—

units.leftText: Everything was verified by number and weight, and the total weight was recorded at that time.
units.rightText: the whole by number and by weight: and all the weight was written at that time.

units.leftText: Then the exiles who had returned from captivity sacrificed burnt offerings to the God of Israel: 12 bulls for all Israel, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and a sin offering of 12 male goats. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: The children of the captivity, that were come out of exile, offered burnt-offerings unto the God of Israel, twelve bullocks for all Israel, ninety and six rams, seventy and seven lambs, twelve he-goats for a sin-offering: all this was a burnt-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: They also delivered the king’s edicts to the royal satraps and governors of the region west of the Euphrates, who proceeded to assist the people and the house of God.
units.rightText: And they delivered the king’s commissions unto the king’s satraps, and to the governors beyond the River: and they furthered the people and the house of God.
leftNotes: 8:36 A satrap was a Persian official.
8:36 Hebrew governors beyond the River

units.leftText: After these things had been accomplished, the leaders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the surrounding peoples whose abominations are like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.
units.rightText: Now when these things were done, the princes drew near unto me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, doing according to their abominations, even of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

units.leftText: Indeed, the Israelites have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land. And the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!”
units.rightText: For they have taken of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the peoples of the lands: yea, the hand of the princes and rulers hath been chief in this trespass.

units.leftText: When I heard this report, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled out some hair from my head and beard, and sat down in horror.
units.rightText: And when I heard this thing, I rent my garment and my robe, and plucked off the hair of my head and of my beard, and sat down confounded.

units.leftText: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat there in horror until the evening offering. Ezra’s Prayer of Confession
units.rightText: Then were assembled unto me every one that trembled at the words of the God of Israel, because of the trespass of them of the captivity; and I sat confounded until the evening oblation.

units.leftText: At the evening offering, I got up from my humiliation with my tunic and cloak torn, and I fell on my knees, spread out my hands to the LORD my God,
units.rightText: And at the evening oblation I arose up from my humiliation, even with my garment and my robe rent; and I fell upon my knees, and spread out my hands unto Jehovah my God;

units.leftText: and said:
units.rightText: and I said, O my God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to thee, my God; for our iniquities are increased over our head, and our guiltiness is grown up unto the heavens.

units.leftText: From the days of our fathers to this day, our guilt has been great. Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth and subjected to the sword and to captivity, to pillage and humiliation, as we are this day.
units.rightText: Since the days of our fathers we have been exceeding guilty unto this day; and for our iniquities have we, our kings, and our priests, been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, and to plunder, and to confusion of face, as it is this day.

units.leftText: But now, for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD our God to preserve for us a remnant and to give us a stake in His holy place. Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.
units.rightText: And now for a little moment grace hath been showed from Jehovah our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and give us a little reviving in our bondage.
leftNotes: 9:8 Or nail or foothold

units.leftText: Though we are slaves, our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but He has extended to us grace in the sight of the kings of Persia, giving us new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins, and giving us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
units.rightText: For we are bondmen; yet our God hath not forsaken us in our bondage, but hath extended lovingkindness unto us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to give us a reviving, to set up the house of our God, and to repair the ruins thereof, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken the commandments
units.rightText: And now, O our God, what shall we say after this? for we have forsaken thy commandments,

units.leftText: that You gave through Your servants the prophets, saying: ‘The land that you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the impurity of its peoples and the abominations with which they have filled it from end to end.
units.rightText: which thou hast commanded by thy servants the prophets, saying, The land, unto which ye go to possess it, is an unclean land through the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, through their abominations, which have filled it from one end to another with their filthiness:

units.leftText: Now, therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may be strong and may eat the good things of the land, leaving it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’
units.rightText: now therefore give not your daughters unto their sons, neither take their daughters unto your sons, nor seek their peace or their prosperity for ever; that ye may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children for ever.

units.leftText: After all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt (though You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this),
units.rightText: And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great guilt, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such a remnant,

units.leftText: shall we again break Your commandments and intermarry with the peoples who commit these abominations? Would You not become so angry with us as to wipe us out, leaving no remnant or survivor?
units.rightText: shall we again break thy commandments, and join in affinity with the peoples that do these abominations? wouldest not thou be angry with us till thou hadst consumed us, so that there should be no remnant, nor any to escape?

units.leftText: O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous! For we remain this day as a remnant. Here we are before You in our guilt, though because of it no one can stand before You.”
units.rightText: O Jehovah, the God of Israel, thou art righteous; for we are left a remnant that is escaped, as it is this day: behold, we are before thee in our guiltiness; for none can stand before thee because of this.

units.leftText: While Ezra prayed and made this confession, weeping and falling facedown before the house of God, a very large assembly of Israelites — men, women, and children — gathered around him, and the people wept bitterly as well.
units.rightText: Now while Ezra prayed and made confession, weeping and casting himself down before the house of God, there was gathered together unto him out of Israel a very great assembly of men and women and children; for the people wept very sore.

units.leftText: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, an Elamite, said to Ezra: “We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the people of the land, yet in spite of this, there is hope for Israel.
units.rightText: And Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, one of the sons of Elam, answered and said unto Ezra, We have trespassed against our God, and have married foreign women of the peoples of the land: yet now there is hope for Israel concerning this thing.

units.leftText: So now let us make a covenant before our God to send away all the foreign wives and their children, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the command of our God. Let it be done according to the Law.
units.rightText: Now therefore let us make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives, and such as are born of them, according to the counsel of my lord, and of those that tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.

units.leftText: Get up, for this matter is your responsibility, and we will support you. Be strong and take action!”
units.rightText: Arise; for the matter belongeth unto thee, and we are with thee: be of good courage, and do it.

units.leftText: So Ezra got up and made the leading priests, Levites, and all Israel take an oath to do what had been said. And they took the oath. The People’s Confession of Sin
units.rightText: Then arose Ezra, and made the chiefs of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel, to swear that they would do according to this word. So they sware.

units.leftText: Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and walked to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. And while he stayed there, he ate no food and drank no water, because he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
units.rightText: Then Ezra rose up from before the house of God, and went into the chamber of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib: and when he came thither, he did eat no bread, nor drink water; for he mourned because of the trespass of them of the captivity.
leftNotes: 10:6 Or went

units.leftText: And a proclamation was issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem that all the exiles should gather at Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And they made proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem unto all the children of the captivity, that they should gather themselves together unto Jerusalem;

units.leftText: Whoever failed to appear within three days would forfeit all his property, according to the counsel of the leaders and elders, and would himself be expelled from the assembly of the exiles.
units.rightText: and that whosoever came not within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and the elders, all his substance should be forfeited, and himself separated from the assembly of the captivity.

units.leftText: So within the three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled in Jerusalem, and on the twentieth day of the ninth month, all the people sat in the square at the house of God, trembling regarding this matter and because of the heavy rain.
units.rightText: Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered themselves together unto Jerusalem within the three days (it was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month); and all the people sat in the broad place before the house of God, trembling because of this matter, and for the great rain.

units.leftText: Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have been unfaithful by marrying foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel.
units.rightText: And Ezra the priest stood up, and said unto them, Ye have trespassed, and have married foreign women, to increase the guilt of Israel.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, make a confession to the LORD, the God of your fathers, and do His will. Separate yourselves from the people of the land and from your foreign wives.”
units.rightText: Now therefore make confession unto Jehovah, the God of your fathers, and do his pleasure; and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land, and from the foreign women.

units.leftText: And the whole assembly responded in a loud voice: “Truly we must do as you say!
units.rightText: Then all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice, As thou hast said concerning us, so must we do.

units.leftText: But there are many people here, and it is the rainy season. We are not able to stay out in the open. Nor is this the work of one or two days, for we have transgressed greatly in this matter.
units.rightText: But the people are many, and it is a time of much rain, and we are not able to stand without: neither is this a work of one day or two; for we have greatly transgressed in this matter.

units.leftText: Let our leaders represent the whole assembly. Then let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at an appointed time, together with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God in this matter is turned away from us.”
units.rightText: Let now our princes be appointed for all the assembly, and let all them that are in our cities that have married foreign women come at appointed times, and with them the elders of every city, and the judges thereof, until the fierce wrath of our God be turned from us, until this matter be despatched.

units.leftText: (Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah, supported by Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite, opposed this plan.)
units.rightText: Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah stood up against this matter: and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.

units.leftText: So the exiles did as proposed. Ezra the priest selected men who were family heads, each of them identified by name, to represent their families. On the first day of the tenth month they launched the investigation,
units.rightText: And the children of the captivity did so. And Ezra the priest, with certain heads of fathers’ houses, after their fathers’ houses, and all of them by their names, were set apart; and they sat down in the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.

units.leftText: and by the first day of the first month they had dealt with all the men who had married foreign women. Those Guilty of Intermarriage
units.rightText: And they made an end with all the men that had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.

units.leftText: Among the descendants of the priests who had married foreign women were found these descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers:
units.rightText: And among the sons of the priests there were found that had married foreign women: namely, of the sons of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and his brethren, Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah.
leftNotes: 10:18 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: They pledged to send their wives away, and for their guilt they presented a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.
units.rightText: And they gave their hand that they would put away their wives; and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their guilt.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, and Elijah, and Shemaiah, and Jehiel, and Uzziah.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.

units.leftText: Among the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
units.rightText: And of the Levites: Jozabad, and Shimei, and Kelaiah (the same is Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.

units.leftText: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
units.rightText: And of the singers: Eliashib. And of the porters: Shallum, and Telem, and Uri.

units.leftText: And among the other Israelites, from the descendants of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
units.rightText: And of Israel: Of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, and Izziah, and Malchijah, and Mijamin, and Eleazar, and Malchijah, and Benaiah.
leftNotes: 10:25 Hebrew; LXX Hashabiah

units.leftText: From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, and Abdi, and Jeremoth, and Elijah.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, and Jeremoth, and Zabad, and Aziza.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, Athlai.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, and Adaiah, Jashub, and Sheal, Jeremoth.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, and Binnui, and Manasseh.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Harim:
units.rightText: And of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,

units.leftText: Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
units.rightText: Benjamin, Malluch, Shemariah.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
units.rightText: Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Bani:
units.rightText: Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, and Uel,

units.leftText: Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,
units.rightText: Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,

units.leftText: Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
units.rightText: Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,

units.leftText: Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu.
units.rightText: Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu,

units.leftText: From the descendants of Binnui:
units.rightText: and Bani, and Binnui, Shimei,

units.leftText: Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,
units.rightText: and Shelemiah, and Nathan, and Adaiah,

units.leftText: Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
units.rightText: Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,

units.leftText: Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
units.rightText: Azarel, and Shelemiah, Shemariah,

units.leftText: Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
units.rightText: Shallum, Amariah, Joseph.

units.leftText: And from the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
units.rightText: Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Iddo, and Joel, Benaiah.

units.leftText: All these men had married foreign women, and some of them had children by these wives.
units.rightText: All these had taken foreign wives; and some of them had wives by whom they had children.
leftNotes: 10:44 Or and they sent them away with their children
